title: MSA/DPA liability slider and automated concession recommendations for sales
creator: Maya Chen
description: Build a lightweight, sales-facing "liability slider" UI and backend recommendation engine that maps common MSA/DPA redline requests (liability caps, indemnity carve-outs, escrow clauses) to a recommended concession and an estimated pricing delta and approval path. Goal: speed up routine negotiations by auto-suggesting acceptable concessions and routing approvals when thresholds are exceeded. This ties into the existing risk-scoring model used by Legal and the Security Questionnaire scoring to reflect technical risk in negotiation tolerances.
acceptance_criteria: Sales UI shows a liability slider with three presets (Standard, Elevated, Enterprise) with clear descriptions and a delta estimate in monthly ARR and one-time legal oversight hours.
Recommendation engine returns: (1) recommended concession language, (2) required approval tier, (3) estimated pricing impact, for 90% of common redline patterns in our dataset.
Route-to-approval integrates with Legal Workbench API: automatic approvals for concessions under Tier 1; email/SMS alert to assigned legal reviewer for Tier 2/3.
Security Questionnaire score (SQS) is factored in: SQS >= 85 reduces default liability by one tier; SQS < 60 increases required approval level.
Telemetry: per-request latency < 350ms 95th percentile, and every recommendation logs decision input, score, and final action (accepted/overridden).
comments: 2025-02-12 Maya Chen: Kickoff — aligned with Legal and Sales Ops on scope. Legal wants three approval tiers and audit trail. Sales wants quick price delta estimate and copyable concession language.
2025-02-18 Liam O'Connor: Met with Pricing to validate ARR delta model. Pricing provided a baseline Excel mapping concessions -> % uplift. Need eng help to codify the model into a microservice.

2025-02-25 Alex Navarro (Legal): Provided canonical concession templates and clarified that indemnity carve-outs require C-level signoff if above $5M cap equivalence. Added list of clauses that must never be auto-approved.
2025-02-28 Design review: Figma mock (file: /design/contracts/liability-slider-v1) received feedback — show both legal exposure and customer benefit in one compact UI. Reduce cognitive load for SDRs.
2025-03-03 ENG sync: Backend will live in contracts-service; ENG-40211 to expose risk-scoring endpoint. Need a feature flag for progressive rollout to 10% of deals.
2025-03-04 Liam O'Connor: Updated spec to include audit log retention requirement (7 years) and opt-in telemetry for pilot customers.
decisions: Pivot to a three-preset slider (Standard/Elevated/Enterprise) rather than continuous numeric slider to simplify Sales training and approvals.
Use existing Legal risk-score model as primary input and augment with Security Questionnaire Score for technical risk adjustments.
Automatic pricing uplift is advisory by default; Sales can accept recommended uplift or override but overrides must capture reason and require manual approval for Tier 3.
Design will expose a 'Why this recommendation?' tooltip that surfaces the top 3 signals (liability clause type, SQS, ARR band) used by the recommendation engine.
Telemetry will feed into Redwood Optimize reporting so product can measure actual uplift capture rate and time-to-sign improvements.
